terms.meaning: A small piece of data the browser stores and sends back with each request, here used to remember the login.
A cookie setting that stops page scripts from reading the cookie, which reduces theft risk.
A signed piece of text that proves a login, created by the session helper.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for sign-in
sections.what: Brings in the request and response tools, password checker, user lookup, session signing, and the cookie name.
sections.why: Keeps each job in its own helper.

sections.name: POST
sections.title: Sign-in handler
sections.what: Handles a sign-in attempt and returns a login cookie when the credentials match.
sections.why: Gives the browser proof of login for later requests.
sections.watch_out: The cookie is marked secure only in production, so production must be served over HTTPS for that protection to apply.

summary: Checks an email and password and, if they match, sets a login cookie that lasts 30 days.
why: Likely reason: lets returning users prove who they are without re-entering invite codes.
how: Reads the email and password, looks up the user, compares the password with the stored hash, creates a signed session token, and stores it in a cookie.
inputs: Email and password in the request body.
outputs: A success message with the email and admin flag, plus the login cookie. Errors: 400 for missing fields, 401 for wrong credentials, 500 for other failures.
risks: No limit on wrong guesses is visible, so password guessing is possible. The email is used as typed, so differences in capital letters may cause a missed match.
debug: A 401 for correct credentials suggests a case mismatch in the email or a stored hash problem. Check getUser in lib/kv and the signing settings in lib/session.
